observation.visible_scene: Nighttime view over a still pond/lake. A wide cluster of dotted spherical firework bursts fills the upper sky above a horizon lined with city lights; the same lights and the bursts appear as long vertical colored reflections on the water. A small boat-like silhouette sits mid-water and a dark platform silhouette sits on the right; a faint grey smoke haze lingers just above the horizon center-right.
visible_changes: The spark dots cycle color across the cluster: predominantly green/white at the start, shifting to pink/red, then to orange-gold with pale blue, reverting to green, and ending with orange-gold on the left and purple/pink on the right.
The spark cloud slowly drifts downward and spreads modestly while keeping its overall wide multi-burst shape; the burst positions are persistent rather than being replaced.
The water reflections change hue in lockstep with the sky, and their vertical streak patterns shimmer and stretch as the colors shift.

The horizon lights, the mid-water boat silhouette, and the right platform silhouette stay in fixed image positions, indicating a static camera; the smoke haze near the horizon remains roughly constant.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch and initial explosion of the shells before t=0 (the bursts are already fully formed at the first frame).
The final fading/dissipation of the sparks after the last frame.
The mechanism behind the color cycling (e.g., shell composition) and the source of the smoke.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight downward movement is true settling or a small perspective/zoom effect (background evidence suggests camera is fixed, so it is likely the sparks themselves).
The exact degree of expansion versus mere drift of the cluster.
Minor shimmer in the reflections could be water motion or color-change artifacts; not separable here.
